'''Russell Edward Morris''' (born 8 June 1967) is a British chemist and Bishop Wardlaw Professor of Chemistry at the [[University of St Andrews]] since 2016.<ref name=stand>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160523103805/https://risweb.st-andrews.ac.uk/portal/en/persons/russell-edward-morris(62d8ade6-032e-40cd-bff9-c6126320ffec).html|archive-date=2016-05-23|url=https://risweb.st-andrews.ac.uk/portal/en/persons/russell-edward-morris(62d8ade6-032e-40cd-bff9-c6126320ffec).html|publisher=st-andrews.ac.uk|location=[[St Andrews]]|title=Professor Russell Edward Morris, FRS FRSE FRSC FLSW: School of Chemistry}}</ref><ref>Russell Morris {{ORCID|0000-0001-7809-0315}}</ref> He played [[first-class cricket]] while he was a student at the [[University of Oxford]],<ref>[http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/17195.html Russell Morris] at [[ESPNcricinfo]]</ref><ref>[https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/12/12161/12161.html Russell Morris] at CricketArchive</ref> and also represented the university in [[association football]] playing in Varsity matches at various venues, including Wembley Stadium and Highbury.

==Education and early life==
Russell Edward Morris was born on 8 June 1967 in [[St Asaph]], Wales, to Merfyn Morris and Ursula Patricia Morris.<ref name=whoswho>{{Who's Who|title=Morris, Prof. Russell Edward|id=U287302|year=2022}}</ref><ref name=aprofile>{{cite journal|title=Author Profile: Russell E. Morris|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|year=2016|doi=10.1002/anie.201601281|last=Morris|first=Russell E.|volume=55|issue=31|page=8794}}</ref> His father Merfyn worked as a plumber in [[Glan Conwy]] in [[North Wales]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.dailypost.co.uk/news/north-wales-news/glan-conwy-plumbers-son-elected-11500318|title=Glan Conwy plumber's son elected as fellow of prestigious Royal Society|last=Jones|first=Mari|date=20 June 2016|work=North Wales Live|access-date=12 April 2023}}</ref> Russell was educated at [[Ysgol Dyffryn Conwy]] in [[Llanrwst]] and went to [[Oriel College, Oxford]], where he was awarded a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree in [[chemistry]] in 1989, followed by a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree in 1992<ref name=whoswho/> for research investigating the synthesis and characterization of metal [[phosphite]]s and [[Selenite (ion)|selenites]], supervised by [[Anthony Cheetham]].<ref>{{cite thesis|degree=DPhil|publisher=University of Oxford|title=Synthesis and characterization of metal phosphites and selenites|first= Russell Edward|last=Morris|date=1992|url=http://solo.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/OXVU1:LSCOP_OX:oxfaleph015968124|oclc=60089703|website=bodleian.ox.ac.uk}}</ref><ref name=MorrisHriljac1990>{{cite journal|last1=Morris|first1=R. E.|last2=Hriljac|first2=J. A.|last3=Cheetham|first3=A. K.|title=Synthesis and crystal structures of two novel selenites, NaY(SeO₃)₂ and NaLa(SeO₃)₂|journal=Acta Crystallographica Section C|volume=46|issue=11|year=1990|pages=2013–2017|issn=0108-2701|doi=10.1107/S0108270190002396|url=http://journals.iucr.org/c/issues/1990/11/00/bw0639/bw0639.pdf}}</ref>

==Research and scientific career==
Morris's research interests lie in the synthesis, characterisation and application of porous and layered materials including [[zeolite]]s<ref name=MazurWheatley2015>{{cite journal|last1=Mazur|first1=Michal|last2=Wheatley|first2=Paul S.|last3=Navarro|first3=Marta|last4=Roth|first4=Wieslaw J.|last5=Položij|first5=Miroslav|last6=Mayoral|first6=Alvaro|last7=Eliášová|first7=Pavla|last8=Nachtigall|first8=Petr|last9=Čejka|first9=Jiří|last10=Morris|first10=Russell E.|title=Synthesis of 'unfeasible' zeolites|journal=[[Nature Chemistry]]|volume=8|issue=1|year=2015|pages=58–62|pmid=26673264|doi=10.1038/nchem.2374|hdl=10023/8675|url=https://research-repository.st-andrews.ac.uk/bitstream/10023/8675/1/Morris_2015_NC_Synthesis_AM.pdf|hdl-access=free}}</ref> and [[metal-organic framework|metal-organic frameworks (MOFs)]].<ref name=HorcajadaGref2012>{{cite journal|last1=Horcajada|first1=Patricia|last2=Gref|first2=Ruxandra|last3=Baati|first3=Tarek|last4=Allan|first4=Phoebe K.|last5=Maurin|first5=Guillaume|last6=Couvreur|first6=Patrick|last7=Férey|first7=Gérard|last8=Morris|first8=Russell E.|author9-link=Christian Serre|last9=Serre|first9=Christian|title=Metal–Organic Frameworks in Biomedicine|journal=[[Chemical Reviews]]|volume=112|issue=2|year=2012|pages=1232–1268|pmid=22168547|doi=10.1021/cr200256v}}</ref> He developed ionothermal synthesis – the use of [[ionic liquid]]s as reactive media for the preparation of solids – a method that has had impact across a wide range of chemistry.<ref name=CooperAndrews2004>{{cite journal|last1=Cooper|first1=Emily R.|last2=Andrews|first2=Christopher D.|last3=Wheatley|first3=Paul S.|last4=Webb|first4=Paul B.|last5=Wormald|first5=Philip|last6=Morris|first6=Russell E.|title=Ionic liquids and eutectic mixtures as solvent and template in synthesis of zeolite analogues|journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]|volume=430|issue=7003|year=2004|pages=1012–1016|doi=10.1038/nature02860|pmid=15329717|bibcode=2004Natur.430.1012C |s2cid=3737160}}</ref> His recent work on developing the assembly–disassembly–organisation–reassembly (ADOR) approach<ref name=WheatleyCejka2016>{{cite journal|last1=Wheatley|first1=Paul S.|last2=Čejka|first2=Jiří|last3=Morris|first3=Russell E.|title=Synthesis of Zeolites Using the ADOR (Assembly-Disassembly-Organization-Reassembly) Route|journal=[[Journal of Visualized Experiments]]|issue=110|article-number=e53463|year=2016|pmid=27078165|pmc=4841360|doi=10.3791/53463}}</ref><ref name=panasenko2015>{{cite journal|last1=Eliášová|first1=Pavla|last2=Opanasenko|first2=Maksym|last3=Wheatley|first3=Paul S.|last4=Shamzhy|first4=Mariya|last5=Mazur|first5=Michal|last6=Nachtigall|first6=Petr|last7=Roth|first7=Wieslaw J.|last8=Morris|first8=Russell E.|last9=Čejka|first9=Jiří|title=The ADOR mechanism for the synthesis of new zeolites|journal=[[Chemical Society Reviews]]|volume=44|issue=20|year=2015|pages=7177–7206|doi=10.1039/C5CS00045A|pmid=25946705|hdl=10023/8734|hdl-access=free}}</ref> to the preparation of zeolites offers routes to exciting materials that would not be possible using standard techniques.

Morris is recognized as a pioneer in the use of [[porous medium|porous materials]] for the storage and delivery of biologically active gases for medical applications.<ref name=frs/><ref name=MorrisWheatley2008>{{cite journal|last1=Morris|first1=Russell E.|last2=Wheatley|first2=Paul S.|title=Gas Storage in Nanoporous Materials|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|volume=47|issue=27|year=2008|pages=4966–4981|pmid=18459091|doi=10.1002/anie.200703934}}</ref>

===Awards and honours===
Morris was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2016|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 2016]].<ref name=frs>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/russell-morris-12886/|title=Professor Russell Morris FRS|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|archive-date=2016-04-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160429121409/https://royalsociety.org/people/russell-morris-12886/|location=London|author=Anon|year=2016}} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{blockquote|"All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]]." --{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies |access-date=2016-03-09 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925220834/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |archive-date=25 September 2015 }}}}</ref> His applications and commercially focused work with MOFgen Ltd.<ref name=mofgen>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160523113628/https://beta.companieshouse.gov.uk/officers/QszJdVvv06FGBnhNJz9dZZN09C0/appointments|archive-date=2016-05-23|url=https://beta.companieshouse.gov.uk/officers/QszJdVvv06FGBnhNJz9dZZN09C0/appointments|title=Russell Edward MORRIS: MOFgen Limited (SC454706)|author=Anon|year=2016|publisher=[[Companies House]]|location=London}}</ref> and [[Sasol]] Technology UK have been recognised by the [[Frank Brian Mercer|Brian Mercer]] Award for Innovation from the [[Royal Society]]. He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh]] (FRSE) in 2008,<ref name=frse>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160330014912/https://www.royalsoced.org.uk/cms/files/fellows/lists/fellows.pdf |archive-date=2016-03-30|url=https://www.royalsoced.org.uk/cms/files/fellows/lists/fellows.pdf |publisher=[[Royal Society of Edinburgh]]|location=Edinburgh|title=Royal Society of Edinburgh Fellows as of 2016-05-13}}</ref> a [[Fellow]] of the [[Learned Society of Wales]] (FLSW) in 2012, and a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry]].{{when|date=May 2016}} In 2019, he was awarded the Tilden Prize by the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Previous winners|url=https://www.rsc.org/prizes-funding/prizes/find-a-prize/tilden-prizes/previous-winners/|access-date=2020-12-17|website=Royal Society of Chemistry|language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Cricket==
Morris was a right-handed [[Batting (cricket)|batsman]] and bowled right-arm [[Seam bowling|medium pace]]. While studying at the [[University of Oxford]], he made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut for [[Oxford University Cricket Club]] in 1987 against [[Hampshire County Cricket Club|Hampshire]]. He made 33 further first-class appearances for the university, the last of which came against [[Cambridge University Cricket Club|Cambridge University]] in the 1991 [[The University Match|University Match]] at [[Lord's]].<ref name="FCM">{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/12/12161/First-Class_Matches.html|title=First-Class Matches played by Russell Morris|publisher=CricketArchive|access-date=11 November 2011}}</ref> In his 34 first-class appearances for Oxford University, he scored 981 runs at an [[batting average (cricket)|average]] of 21.32, with a high score of 96.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/12/12161/f_Batting_by_Team.html|title=First-class Batting and Fielding For Each Team by Russell Morris|publisher=CricketArchive|access-date=11 November 2011}}</ref> This score, which was one of eight [[Century (cricket)|fifties]] he made for the university, came against [[Surrey County Cricket Club|Surrey]] at the [[University Parks]] in 1990.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/52/52715.html|title=Oxford University v Surrey, 1990|publisher=CricketArchive|access-date=11 November 2011}}</ref> The same year, he also appeared once for a combined [[Oxford and Cambridge Universities cricket team|Oxford and Cambridge Universities side]] against the touring [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealanders]].<ref name="FCM"/> He batted with success in this match: [[captain (cricket)|captaining]] the side, he scored 75 in the team's first innings before being dismissed by [[John Bracewell]], while in the team's second innings, he scored 53 before being dismissed by the same bowler.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/53/53028.html|title=Oxford and Cambridge Universities v New Zealanders, 1990|publisher=CricketArchive|access-date=11 November 2011}}</ref>

While studying at Oxford, Morris was also a part of the [[British Universities cricket team|Combined Universities]] team in the 1991 [[Benson and Hedges Cup]].<ref name="lista"/> He made four [[List A cricket|List A]] appearances during the competition, against [[Gloucestershire County Cricket Club|Gloucestershire]], [[Derbyshire County Cricket Club|Derbyshire]], [[Worcestershire County Cricket Club|Worcestershire]] and [[Northamptonshire County Cricket Club|Northamptonshire]].<ref name="lista">{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/12/12161/List_A_Matches.html|title=List A Matches played by Russell Morris|publisher=CricketArchive|access-date=11 November 2011}}</ref> In these four matches, he scored 44 runs at an average of 11.00, with a high score of 19.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/12/12161/a_Batting_by_Team.html|title=List A Batting and Fielding For Each Team by Russell Morris|publisher=CricketArchive|access-date=11 November 2011}}</ref>

Morris also played for [[Wales Minor Counties Cricket Club|Wales Minor Counties]] in the [[Minor Counties Championship]], making two appearances in 1990 against [[Dorset County Cricket Club|Dorset]] and [[Wiltshire County Cricket Club|Wiltshire]] and one appearance in 1991 against Dorset.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/12/12161/Minor_Counties_Championship_Matches.html|title=Minor Counties Championship Matches played by Russell Morris|publisher=CricketArchive|access-date=11 November 2011}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Morris married Silke Frauke Karen Wewetzer in 2002. They have a son and a daughter.<ref name=whoswho/>
